This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to
  reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to AB 361
  and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order
  (revised April 21, 2022). All votes taken during this
  teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will
  be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which
will be live streamed at https://MalibuCity.org/Video and https://MalibuCity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged
to submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item
you would like to speak on has been called and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to
speak and to download the Zoom application.

Subject:  Update on Santa Monica College Malibu Campus and Los Angeles
  County Sheriff Substation

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file an update on the Santa Monica College
Malibu Campus and Los Angeles County Sheriff Substation project. This project is not
funded by the City of Malibu.

DISCUSSION: The satellite campus is a two-story building that includes classrooms,
science and computer labs, a lecture hall, an art studio, study space, an interpretive
center, a multipurpose room, a conference room, offices, and 179 parking spaces. The
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department will occupy a one-story wing of the building.
The multipurpose room, also to be open to the Malibu community, will be shared by the
Sheriff’s Department and SMC. The project employs various sustainability strategies,
including low water consumption fixtures, the use of reclaimed water for irrigation, green
building materials, and equipment commissioning. The project is anticipated to receive
LEED Gold Certification. The estimated completion date for this project is November
2022.

Construction Update. Charlie Yen, Director, Facilities Planning, will provide an updated
presentation of progress on the project and will be available to answer questions.

To:  Malibu Public Facilities Authority Commissioners

Prepared by:  Don Girard, Senior Director, Government Relations & Institutional

Date prepared:  July 20, 2022  Meeting date: July 28, 2022

Subject:  Santa Monica College Malibu Campus Programming

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update and provide additional feedback on
Santa Monica College’s (SMC) evaluation of programming opportunities based on an
ongoing assessment of community interest in educational programs and hosted events at
the new SMC Malibu Campus.

BACKGROUND: SMC prepared an online survey to assess community interest in SMC’s
range of educational offerings, which include credit classes, noncredit classes, Emeritus
classes, and community education classes. The online survey launched in late March.

Information about the online survey was mailed to approximately 60,000 Malibu and
Malibu-area residents and businesses and promoted through ads in local newspapers,
including the Malibu Times, the Acorn (Agoura), the Canyon Chronicle (Topanga), and a
series of online ads through the Pepperdine Graphic. The survey was also promoted in
email communications from the Malibu Chamber of Commerce and from the City of
Malibu’s Public Information Office. Over 600 responses to the online survey have been
received as of the date of this report.

The online survey can be found at SMC.edu/MalibuSurvey.

SMC has begun its educational planning based on results of the survey and will further
develop its planning based on additional community input and the availability of instructors.

DISCUSSION:  Courses were identified through the community survey, focusing mostly
on classes where a significant number of respondents indicated that they, themselves,
would be interested in enrolling. A potential spring 2023 schedule has been developed
that could include up to ten sections of credit classes, twelve sections of Emeritus

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 4.B.
 noncredit classes, an additional three noncredit classes, and five community education
classes.

The credit classes would cover first-year coursework in the subject areas of biology,
botany, communication studies (speech), English, film, yoga, math, psychology, and
dance. Noncredit courses would include an ESL class in partnership with Pepperdine,
CPR certification, and early childhood education.

Emeritus classes would include t’ai chi, figure drawing, an intergenerational art class,
poetry and fiction, creative writing, autobiography, survey of art, drawing, drawing and
painting, current events, music, and introduction to acting. Community education classes
would cover such areas as vocal yoga, architectural lectures, barre body workouts, and
painting.

SMC is also exploring events to be hosted at the campus, some to be presented by the
college and others in partnership with community organizations. Various options will be
presented by staff.

Current planning envisions the campus hours to be 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday
through Friday, with some weekend use of the campus for events.

ATTACHMENTS: None.

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Update on Santa Monica College Malibu Campus and Los Angeles County
  Sheriff Sub-Station
  Recommended Action: Receive and file an update on the Santa Monica
  College (SMC) Malibu Campus and Los Angeles County Sheriff Sub-
  Station project. This project is not funded by the City of Malibu.

  SMC Director Yen provided a presentation on the status of the project.

  In response to Commissioner Silverstein, Mr. Yen stated the irrigation
  would connect to the City’s system for recycled water. In response to
  Commissioner Silverstein, Mr. Yen stated the color of the communication
  tower was dictated by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). He
  stated the tower belonged to and would be operated by the County of Los
  Angeles.

  In response to Chair Greenstein, Mr. Yen stated the patio space on the
  second floor was under cover but open to the environment. He stated there
  would be tables and chairs, probably large enough for about 20 students.

  Commissioner Silverstein stated that with the the project looked beautiful,
  except for the tower.

  B.  Santa Monica College Malibu Campus Programming
  Recommended Action: Receive an update and provide additional feedback
  on Santa Monica College’s (SMC) evaluation of programming
  opportunities based on an ongoing assessment of community interest in
  educational programs and hosted events at the new SMC Malibu Campus.

  SMC Senior Director Girard introduced Scott Silverman, Associate Dean,
  who presented the report and discussed responses to the survey of and
   Malibu Public Facilities Authority
  Minutes of July 28, 2022
  Page 3 of 4
  __________________________

  community meetings with Malibu residents. He stated there would be
  approximately 30 classes offered at the campus in Spring 2023, including
  credit classes, non-credit classes, Emeritus classes, and community
  education classes. He stated specific classes were still being developed and
  should be available by November. He stated possible events were being
  considered for scheduling in Spring 2023 or saved for Summer 2023 and
  beyond.

  In response to Commissioner Grisanti, Ms. Davis stated Spring classes
  would being February 13, 2023. Dr. Silverman stated Spring enrollment
  would begin in November.

  Ms. Davis stated SMC was very excited about the variety of classes and
  how the different rooms would be used. Dr. Silverman stated classes would
  primarily be 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. with some in later afternoon, at least
  for the first semester.

  In response to Commissioner Greenstein, Dr. Silverman discussed the
  feedback from the community on the survey.

  Commissioner Greenstein stated she looked forward to a tour of the
  buildings.

ITEM 1B  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Quińones-Perez commended staff for getting through the
  barriers and delays. She stated she was very proud of the project and the
  development of programming.

  Commissioner Greenstein stated the College was very excited to move into
  Malibu.

  In response to Commissioner Greenstein, Commissioner Grisanti stated
  many members of the community were previously unaware of the project
  and were excited to see the new building. He agreed with Commissioner
  Silverstein that many community members were not happy about the tower.

  Commissioner Greenstein stated she was excited to hear someone from the
  Malibu community express appreciation for the beautiful building.

  Commissioner Quińones-Perez stated it has been an awesome partnership.

  In response to Malibu Executive Assistant Linden, Commissioner
  Quińones-Perez and Commissioner Greenstein stated it would be best to
  schedule the next meeting in October 2022.
